solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Notice argument lost (6)

blocks.note: an ad is a notice, as in a newspaper

annotation.surface: A notice about a quarrel has gone missing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Notice' reads as a verb, but it is the noun AD; 'lost' sits at the end as the definition, in the sense of drifting without direction.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone adrift is lost, without bearings.

entries.clue: Short, a theatrical work (5)

blocks.note: a short is a small measure of spirits, a dram

annotation.surface: Something brief described as a piece of theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like an adjective, but in Britain a short is a small shot of spirits, and a dram is exactly that.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: any play written for the stage counts.

entries.clue: Popular castle I rebuilt, changing very little (9)

indicators.note: the letters of CASTLE I are put together again in a new order

annotation.surface: A well-loved castle restored with hardly any alterations.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a sympathetic restoration; the definition is the economist's sense, as in demand that is inelastic, barely changing when price does.
annotation.definitionFit: Something inelastic does not stretch or respond, so it changes very little.

entries.clue: Drink container that’s half open tipped up into baby feeder (6)

indicators.note: only half of OPEN is used, OP
in a down clue, tipping OP up turns it to PO
'into' means going inside something, so PO is put inside TEAT

blocks.note: the teat of a baby's bottle

annotation.surface: A drinks vessel with its lid half open, being tipped into a baby's bottle.
annotation.walkthrough: TEA(PO)T: the surface pictures the pot itself being tipped, which is apt, since that is how a teapot is used.
annotation.definitionFit: Literal description: the vessel is named for the drink it holds.

entries.clue: Month before series seen on English writer (8)

indicators.note: 'before' means earlier in time, and in an across answer earlier means further left, so the month opens the word
something seen on a thing is placed against it; in an across clue the series follows English

blocks.note: NOV is the calendar abbreviation for November
a list is a series of items

annotation.surface: A month's run of articles appearing about an English author.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Series' tempts as a TV run to pair with 'writer', but it is just a list; 'English' gives its usual single letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Writer is the broader class; a novelist is one kind of writer, a definition by genus.

entries.clue: Less prestige, all the same (15)

blocks.note: less, as in minus, means without: not with

annotation.surface: Losing status makes no difference in the end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Less prestige' is read as 'not with standing', three words run together into one long adverb.
annotation.definitionFit: Notwithstanding, used as an adverb, means nevertheless or all the same.

entries.clue: Leader in Victoria, queen opening alcoholic drink (8)

indicators.note: the leader of Victoria is its first letter, V

annotation.surface: A monarch, first among Victorians, cracking open a bottle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Victoria' and 'queen' pull together toward royalty, but only Victoria's first letter is used, and the queen is ER.
annotation.definitionFit: Vermouth is a fortified wine flavoured with herbs.

entries.clue: Upset fiend settled (5)

indicators.note: to upset something is to knock it over, and in a down clue that turns the word upside down

annotation.surface: A demon, once agitated, has calmed down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Settled' tempts as the opposite of 'upset', but here it means lived, as in settled somewhere.
annotation.definitionFit: Settled in the sense of made a home somewhere; the definition matches in tense as a past verb.

entries.clue: Country where a Norman is lost (3,6)

indicators.note: the letters of A NORMAN IS have lost their way into a new order

annotation.surface: A land where a Norman wanders without bearings.
annotation.walkthrough: San Marino is a tiny republic inside Italy, a place a medieval Norman might well have lost his way.
annotation.definitionFit: San Marino is an independent country, one of the smallest in Europe.

entries.clue: Leading man, say, arresting female felon (10)

indicators.note: to arrest is to seize and hold, so the outer word holds the female inside it

blocks.note: a leading man is one example of a male actor

annotation.surface: A film's leading man detaining a female criminal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks the leading man as only one example of the wider class; 'arresting' fits the crime story but just means holding inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from the Latin for evil-doer; it also sits neatly with the arrest in the surface.

entries.clue: Number after six, red or white? (4)

indicators.note: 'after' means following, so in an across answer the number sits to the right of six

blocks.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: Choosing between red or white wine just after six o'clock.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: red and white are kinds of wine.
annotation.definitionFit: Vino is informal for wine, which comes red or white.

entries.clue: Italian food in a can, or I’m fresh (8)

indicators.note: a fresh arrangement of A CAN OR I'M

annotation.surface: Pasta available either tinned or freshly made.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface offers canned or fresh pasta; 'fresh' is the only instruction, and the fodder runs across the comma.
annotation.definitionFit: Macaroni is a tube-shaped Italian pasta.

entries.clue: Road he designed that’s a disappointment! (2,4)

indicators.note: to design something is to plan its layout, so the letters get a new arrangement

annotation.surface: An engineer's new road turns out a letdown.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is an exclamation, so the answer is a phrase someone says rather than a noun for disappointment.
annotation.definitionFit: Oh dear is what someone says on meeting a disappointment.

entries.clue: Practice won’t start for an hour or so? (1,3)

indicators.note: HABIT loses its first letter

annotation.surface: A rehearsal delayed by an hour or so.
annotation.walkthrough: The dropped letter is H, the standard abbreviation for hour, which the definition then names; the question mark flags an hour or so as one example of a bit.
annotation.definitionFit: A bit can mean a short while, and an hour or so is one.

entries.clue: Talented player batting, a graceful performer (9)

blocks.note: a baller is slang for a skilled sports player
the side batting in cricket is in

annotation.surface: A gifted cricketer at the crease, moving with grace.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side is said to be 'in'; the surface stays on the sports field until the dancer appears.
annotation.definitionFit: A ballerina is a ballet dancer, a performer known for grace.

entries.clue: Thai meal ruined, something poisonous delivered? (4,4)

indicators.note: THAI MEAL is wrecked into a new order

annotation.surface: A takeaway Thai dinner spoiled, as if it were poisoned on delivery.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a bad food delivery; the definition shifts 'poisonous' to venomous words sent through the post.
annotation.definitionFit: Hate mail is abusive letters, poisonous in tone and delivered to the victim.

entries.clue: Alakazam, please? (5,4)

blocks.note: what parents prompt a child to say before they get something

annotation.walkthrough: Parents ask 'What's the magic word?' to prompt a child to say please; the question mark nods at that second, playful sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Alakazam is a magician's spell word, and please is the polite 'magic word'.

entries.clue: Cave in woodland area entered by everyone from below (8)

indicators.note: COPSE is entered by the other part, which goes inside it
in a down clue, ALL read from below gives LLA

blocks.note: a copse is a small wood

annotation.surface: A cave in the woods that everyone crawls into from underneath.
annotation.walkthrough: CO(LLA)PSE: 'Cave' looks like a noun in a woodland scene, but 'Cave in' is a verb meaning give way.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb and its plain synonym: a roof or tunnel that caves in falls down.

entries.clue: Miss during fight when the lights are off (8)

indicators.note: what happens during an event happens within it, so the miss goes inside the fight

blocks.note: a bout is a boxing match
to miss something is to lack it

annotation.surface: A boxer misses a punch mid-bout when the arena lights fail.
annotation.walkthrough: B(LACK)OUT: 'Miss' reads as a missed punch, but it is the verb lack.
annotation.definitionFit: A blackout is a period when the lights are out, from a power cut or by order.

entries.clue: Thug, I’m encouraging you! (4)

blocks.note: a hired heavy, a slang word
a two-word cry urging someone to proceed

annotation.surface: Someone egging on a hoodlum.
annotation.walkthrough: The enumeration is a single word of 4 letters, so the same letters read as GOON and as GO ON.
annotation.definitionFit: A goon is a thug, and 'Go on!' is a cry of encouragement.

entries.clue: Mark secures lead on rare breed (6)

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the mark holds the letter inside it
the lead on 'rare' is its first letter

annotation.surface: A dog owner, Mark, puts a lead on a rare-breed dog.
annotation.walkthrough: ST(R)AIN: the surface is dog-walking with a lead, but the lead is just the first letter of 'rare'.
annotation.definitionFit: A strain is a breed or variety of animal or plant.

entries.clue: Worse than hazardous, all the liquid (6)

indicators.note: liquid letters flow into a new shape

annotation.surface: A warning that the whole liquid is more than just dangerous.
annotation.walkthrough: 'liquid' reads as a noun at the end of a hazard label, but it is an adjective telling the letters of ALL THE to flow.
annotation.definitionFit: Lethal means deadly, a step beyond merely hazardous.

entries.clue: Reddish-brown liquid then naturally bottled (5)

indicators.note: the answer is held inside 'then naturally', like liquid in a bottle

annotation.surface: A reddish-brown fluid that was then bottled without additives.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer sits across two words: tHEN NAturally.
annotation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish-brown dye, used as a paste or liquid on hair and skin.

entries.clue: Observe example in wallet (8)

annotation.surface: Look at this specimen found inside a wallet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'in' sounds like a container instruction, but nothing goes inside anything: it only links wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A notecase is an old-fashioned word for a wallet for banknotes.

entries.clue: Failing American in hole (5)

blocks.note: a failing is a moral fault, a sin

annotation.surface: An American who has come unstuck and ended up in a hole.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Failing' reads as a verb, but it is the noun, a moral failing or sin.
annotation.definitionFit: A sinus is a cavity, such as the air-filled holes in the skull.

entries.clue: European pub on Friday’s opening (4)

indicators.note: in an across clue, INN sits on F by following it
Friday's opening is its first letter, F

annotation.surface: A European heads to the pub as the weekend opens on Friday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'European' is a broad definition; the wordplay narrows it to one nationality.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: someone from Finland is one kind of European.

entries.clue: Rip off pop star, diva (5,5)

indicators.note: RIP goes off, out of order, to give PRI

annotation.surface: Someone copying a famous pop diva.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rip off' reads as one phrase meaning copy, but it splits: 'off' scrambles RIP, and the pop star is Madonna.
annotation.definitionFit: A prima donna is the lead female opera singer, and by extension a temperamental diva.

entries.clue: Fail – as might turkey? (3,2,3)

blocks.note: slang, chiefly American, for a show or performance flopping

annotation.walkthrough: A turkey is also slang for a flop, so the second definition doubles back on the first; the question mark marks the playful literal reading.
annotation.definitionFit: To lay an egg is to fail badly, especially on stage, and a turkey is a bird that lays eggs.

entries.clue: Sun worshipper in sun, tide endlessly turning (6)

indicators.note: TIDE loses its last letter, TID
SUN and TID are turned into a new order

blocks.note: sun as printed, then TIDE without its last letter: anagram fodder, 6 letters

annotation.surface: A sunbather on the beach as the tide turns.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sun worshipper' suggests a pagan, but it is someone who strips off to sunbathe.
annotation.definitionFit: A nudist takes off everything, often to worship the sun on a beach.
